title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 14.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Asa did that which was good and right
Asa took away altars of strange gods
Asa commanded Judah to seek the LORD God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:1 states first that Abijah slept with his fathers and was buried, then Asa reigned in his stead.

questions.question: Who reigned in place of Abijah according to 2 Chronicles 14?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:1 states that Asa, his son, reigned in his stead.

questions.question: For how many years was the land quiet during Asa's reign as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 14?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:1 says the land was quiet ten years in his days.

questions.question: What did Asa do in the eyes of the LORD his God according to 2 Chronicles 14?
options: Did that which was good and right
questions.correctAnswer: Did that which was good and right
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:2 states Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the LORD.

questions.question: Which of the following did Asa take away from Judah as recorded in 2 Chronicles 14?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:3 says Asa took away the altars of the strange gods.

questions.question: What else did Asa break down besides altars according to 2 Chronicles 14?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:3 states Asa broke down the images.

questions.question: What did Asa cut down as part of his reforms according to 2 Chronicles 14?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:3 states Asa cut down the groves.

questions.question: What did Asa command Judah to do in 2 Chronicles 14?
options: Seek the LORD God of their fathers
questions.correctAnswer: Seek the LORD God of their fathers
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:4 says Asa commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers.

questions.question: Besides seeking the LORD, what else did Asa command Judah to do?
options: Do the law and the commandment
Build altars on the high places
questions.correctAnswer: Do the law and the commandment
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:4 states Asa also commanded them to do the law and the commandment.

questions.question: What did Asa remove from all the cities of Judah according to 2 Chronicles 14?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:5 says Asa took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the images.

questions.question: How was the kingdom described during Asa's reign in 2 Chronicles 14?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:5 states the kingdom was quiet before Asa.

questions.question: True or False: Asa reigned after Abijah according to 2 Chronicles 14.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:1 states Asa his son reigned in his stead after Abijah.

questions.question: True or False: Asa commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers and to do the law and the commandment.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:4 clearly states Asa commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers and to do the law and commandment.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 14, Asa built new altars for strange gods to worship.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:3 states Asa took away the altars of strange gods, not built them.

questions.question: True or False: Asa's reign was marked by many wars according to 2 Chronicles 14.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:1 and 14:5 state the land and kingdom were quiet during Asa's reign, indicating no wars.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Asa build in Judah during the years of rest?
questions.explanation: Asa built fenced cities in Judah because the land had rest, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:6.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 14:7 promise will happen if someone seeks the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:7 states that because they sought the LORD, they built and prospered.

questions.question: How many men did Asa have in his army from Judah?
questions.explanation: Asa had an army of 300,000 men that bare targets and spears from Judah, as noted in 2 Chronicles 14:8.

questions.question: What did Asa do when Zerah the Ethiopian came against them?
questions.explanation: Asa went out against Zerah the Ethiopian when he came with a great host, as described in 2 Chronicles 14:10.

questions.question: What was the size of Zerah's army?
questions.explanation: Zerah came with a host of a thousand thousand, which is 1,000,000 men, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:9.

questions.question: What did Asa command Judah to do according to 2 Chronicles 14:4?
questions.explanation: Asa commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:4.

questions.question: What was the result of Asa's good actions as stated in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The land was quiet for ten years during Asa's reign because he did what was good in the eyes of the LORD, as noted in 2 Chronicles 14:1.

questions.question: What did Asa take away from Judah according to 2 Chronicles 14:3?
questions.explanation: Asa took away the altars of strange gods and the high places, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 14:3.

questions.question: What did Asa's actions lead to in Judah as described in the verses?
questions.explanation: Because Asa sought the LORD, the land had rest and there was no war in those years, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:6.

questions.question: What significant military strategy did Asa undertake?
questions.explanation: Asa set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah against Zerah, as described in 2 Chronicles 14:10.

questions.question: What was Asa’s motivation for building cities according to 2 Chronicles 14:7?
questions.explanation: Asa built the cities because they had sought the LORD, who had given them rest on every side, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:7.

questions.question: Did Asa have a larger army from Judah or Benjamin?
questions.explanation: Asa had 300,000 men from Judah, which is larger than the 280,000 from Benjamin, as noted in 2 Chronicles 14:8.

questions.question: Is it true that Asa commanded Judah to worship strange gods?
questions.explanation: Asa commanded Judah to seek the LORD and to do the law and the commandment, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:4, which is contrary to worshiping strange gods.

questions.question: Is it true that Zerah brought an army of 1 million men against Asa?
questions.explanation: Zerah the Ethiopian came against Asa with an army of a thousand thousand men, which equals 1 million, according to 2 Chronicles 14:9.

questions.question: Is it true that Asa had no military preparation before Zerah attacked?
questions.explanation: Asa had built an army and prepared for battle, as seen in 2 Chronicles 14:8 where it details his military strength.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 14.

questions.question: What did Asa cry out to the LORD for in his prayer?
questions.explanation: Asa cried unto the LORD, asking for help against the multitude of Ethiopians. This is stated in 2 Chronicles 14:11.

questions.question: What was the outcome of Asa's battle against the Ethiopians?
questions.explanation: The LORD smote the Ethiopians before Asa and Judah, leading to their victory, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 14:12.

questions.question: What did Asa and his people pursue after defeating the Ethiopians?
questions.explanation: Asa and the people pursued the Ethiopians after they fled, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:13.

questions.question: What did Asa and his men carry away after their victory?
questions.explanation: They carried away sheep and camels in abundance after smiting the tents of cattle, as per 2 Chronicles 14:15.

questions.question: What caused the fear of the LORD to come upon the cities around Gerar?
questions.explanation: The fear of the LORD came upon them after Asa's victory over the Ethiopians, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:14.

questions.question: How many men did Asa have in his army from Judah?
questions.explanation: Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 14:8.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'help' in 2 Chronicles 14:11 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'help' implies the action of delivering or saving, as Asa sought divine intervention.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Asa's prayer in 2 Chronicles 14:11?
questions.explanation: Asa's prayer exhibits parallelism by contrasting 'with many' and 'with them that have no power' to emphasize God's capability.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Asa's reliance on God in battle?
questions.explanation: Psalm 20:7 states, 'Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God.' This echoes Asa's dependence on God.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of victory through divine intervention?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 14:10 recounts God’s assurance to David that He would go before him in battle, similar to Asa's experience.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Asa's prayer in 2 Chronicles 14:11?
options: The description of the Ethiopian army
The building of cities in Judah
The command to seek the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The description of the Ethiopian army
questions.explanation: Before Asa's prayer, the verse describes the large host of Zerah the Ethiopian that came against them, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:9.

questions.question: What did Asa do prior to engaging in battle with the Ethiopians?
questions.explanation: Asa built cities, sought the LORD, and prepared his army, showing his comprehensive preparation as recorded in 2 Chronicles 14:7-8.

questions.question: Asa's actions in removing strange gods illustrate what theme?
questions.explanation: Asa removed strange gods, demonstrating covenant faithfulness and judgment against idolatry, as stated in 2 Chronicles 14:3.

questions.question: True or False: Asa reigned for ten years without war due to God's favor.
questions.explanation: Asa reigned in a time of peace for ten years because the LORD had given him rest, as noted in 2 Chronicles 14:1.

questions.question: True or False: Asa's army consisted of only 100,000 men.
questions.explanation: Asa's army was much larger, comprising 500,000 men in total, as detailed in 2 Chronicles 14:8.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 14:2 teach about human sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves active obedience to God's standards
Sanctification is an instantaneous event without ongoing effort
Sanctification is primarily about external rituals
Sanctification depends on human wisdom alone
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves active obedience to God's standards
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 14:2 states that Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD, emphasizing active and continual obedience as part of sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 14:4 teach about covenant faithfulness and law?
options: Covenant faithfulness requires seeking God and obeying His law
Covenant faithfulness is guaranteed without obedience
Law obedience is optional for covenant members
Seeking God alone is sufficient without law observance
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness requires seeking God and obeying His law
questions.explanation: Verse 4 commands Judah to seek the LORD God and to do the law and the commandment, showing that covenant faithfulness is both relational and obedient.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine providence does 2 Chronicles 14:6 teach?
options: God grants peace and rest to His people as a sign of His providential care
God is indifferent to the peace of nations
Peace results solely from human military strength
Providence operates independently of human seeking
questions.correctAnswer: God grants peace and rest to His people as a sign of His providential care
questions.explanation: Verse 6 notes that the land had rest and no war because the LORD had given him rest, indicating God's providential granting of peace.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 14:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows the LORD smiting the Ethiopians, demonstrating God's sovereign power over nations and battles.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 14:11 highlight in Asa's prayer?
questions.explanation: In verse 11, Asa acknowledges that it is nothing for God to help with many or with the weak, highlighting God's omnipotence.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 14:1 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine blessing upon obedience?
options: It illustrates that God grants peace when His people follow His ways
It teaches that peace is unrelated to obedience
It shows peace is a result of political alliances
It emphasizes human effort over divine blessing
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates that God grants peace when His people follow His ways
questions.explanation: Verse 1 notes the land was quiet for ten years during Asa's reign, setting a pattern where divine blessing follows obedience to God.

questions.question: How does the battle in 2 Chronicles 14:10-13 foreshadow Christ's victory over spiritual enemies?
options: The Lord's direct intervention and complete victory prefigure Christ's triumph over evil
It shows human armies winning without divine help
It depicts a temporary political victory with no spiritual significance
It emphasizes military technology over divine power
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord's direct intervention and complete victory prefigure Christ's triumph over evil
questions.explanation: Verses 10-13 recount the LORD smiting the Ethiopians and their utter defeat, symbolizing God's ultimate victory in Christ over spiritual foes.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 14:3 and 14:5 teach about idolatry and sanctification?
options: True sanctification requires removing idols and false worship completely
Idolatry is tolerable if accompanied by some worship of God
Sanctification is unrelated to external worship practices
Idolatry is not addressed in sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: True sanctification requires removing idols and false worship completely
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 5 show Asa removing altars, images, and high places, teaching that sanctification entails purging idolatry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 14:7 and 14:6 teach about human responsibility and God's provision in peace?
options: God grants rest, but humans must build and secure in faith
God grants rest without human effort
Peace depends only on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: God grants rest, but humans must build and secure in faith
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows God gave rest, and verse 7 shows Asa urging building cities and defenses, combining divine provision with human responsibility.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 14:11 and 14:12 teach about prayer and divine intervention?
options: God answers prayer by sovereignly delivering His people in battle
Divine intervention is random and unrelated to prayer
Victory depends on human tactics alone
questions.correctAnswer: God answers prayer by sovereignly delivering His people in battle
questions.explanation: Verse 11 records Asa's prayer for help, and verse 12 describes God's delivering the Ethiopians to Judah, showing answered prayer.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the peace in Judah was due solely to military power and not divine aid. What does 2 Chronicles 14:8-12 actually teach?
options: The text teaches divine aid was decisive despite military numbers
The text credits military power alone for peace
The text denies any divine involvement
The text attributes peace to political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: The text teaches divine aid was decisive despite military numbers
questions.explanation: Verses 8-12 show Asa's large army faced a greater foe but victory came after prayer and divine intervention, proving God's power over mere numbers.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 14:15 teach about God's blessing and material provision?
options: God blesses His people materially as a sign of favor and victory
Material blessing is unrelated to divine favor
Victory spoils are a result of human greed
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses His people materially as a sign of favor and victory
questions.explanation: Verse 15 describes the spoils taken abundantly, indicating God's blessing in material provision after victory.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 14:7 best demonstrate in the context of human and divine cooperation?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 emphasizes that because they sought the LORD, He gave them rest, showing God's faithfulness to covenant promises.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 14:9 and 14:13 teach about spiritual warfare and God's judgment on enemies?
options: God judges and defeats enemies who oppose His people
Enemies triumph due to human failure
Conflict is purely political with no spiritual dimension
questions.correctAnswer: God judges and defeats enemies who oppose His people
questions.explanation: Verse 9 introduces Zerah's invasion, and verse 13 shows their destruction by God’s hand, teaching divine judgment in spiritual warfare.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 14:14 teach about the fear of the LORD as a theological principle for societal order?
options: The fear of the LORD instills societal submission and order
Fear of God causes chaos and rebellion
Societal order is independent of divine fear
Fear of the LORD is irrelevant to political stability
questions.correctAnswer: The fear of the LORD instills societal submission and order
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states the fear of the LORD came upon the cities causing them to be smitten and spoiled, showing how reverence for God enforces societal order.
